6. I don't know what I watched, but it made me smile. Dylan Cardwell is a complete experience. He runs the floor. He goes vertical at the rim. He fouls everyone. But when he gets an opportunity to throw down a dunk, he makes sure everyone in the building knows it happened. Play your game.

5. Got a shot. With De'Andre Hunter out with an illness, Doug Christie turned to Leaky Black as his starting small forward. Black is interesting. He plays hard, but under control and he's always ready to launch the 3-ball. He finished with 12 points, 5 assists, 3 rebounds and 2 steals.

4. Rounding into shape. It's taken some time, but Malik Monk is really starting to look like himself again. He hit the Spurs for 12 points on an efficient 3-for-6 from the field and he added 7 assists in 18 minutes. Monk is giving the Kings that secondary playmaker they desperately need.

3. So confident. Emanuel Sharp is locked and loaded on every possession. He doesn't even look like he's ready to shoot most of the time, but it lands in his hands and he's already hoisting. The rookie scored 9 points on 3-for-4 from deep and provided defensive agitation.

2. So many looks. The Spurs have one star level guard after another and they threw them all at Darius Acuff Jr. The rookie took a while to make adjustments, but he still managed to get it rolling. He finished with 22 points on 9-for-20 shooting to go with 8 assists.
